title: RSA mapping of integers to fixed-length octet strings
summary: OS2IP reads a big-endian octet string as a nonnegative integer. I2OSP emits the requested number of octets, with leading zero bytes as needed.
applies: Byte representation and parameter explanation of cryptography questions
detail: 00 01 and 01 are both integers 1 via OS2IP; only I2OSP(1,2) will restore 00 01.
boundary: Converting to an integer will lose the original length; if the integer does not fit into the given width, I2OSP will report an error.
relevance: When comparing the same record in integer form and hexadecimal form, the byte width corresponding to the modulus is preserved.
